notes: The new standing-height three-quarter camera and shared gunmetal floor/canopy surface make the fabrication deck read as a contained room with real depth. The canopy edge remains abrupt and the foreground floor still consumes too much of the frame.

The opposite-side capture holds a continuous rear and side equipment perimeter, but repeated workstation modules remain sparse, evenly spaced, and visibly procedural beside the dense yacht workshop reference.

The rotary service subject and overhead handling system stay legible from both interior angles. The paired manipulators are oversized relative to the room and their low-segment joints dominate the composition.

Warm longitudinal coves now reveal fore-aft continuity in the bowed canopy and the alternate angle verifies a real pressure volume. Structural thickness, panel seams, edge bevels, and glass-to-frame transitions are still too weak.

A workshop-only clear-coated gunmetal finish and dedicated amber floor wash recover the floor from near-black and preserve the bronze/cyan palette. Large surfaces remain textureless, floor inlays read mostly as reflections, and the lighting lacks the reference's layered practicals and contact response.
